exposure: Various neonatal interventions (e.g., endotracheal intubation, antibiotics)
End-organ damage (EOD) vs. no end-organ damage (NEOD)
outcome: Clinical outcomes (cure, improvement, death, withdrawal from treatment)
cohort: 223 neonates with IFI treated in a tertiary NICU in China between January 2009 and December 2022
finding: Preterm infants, particularly very preterm infants, were highly susceptible to fungal infections, with C. albicans being the most common pathogen and a significant risk factor for EOD, leading to poorer clinical outcomes.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the rate of premature birth or mode of delivery between neonates who did and did not experience end-organ damage related to invasive fungal infection.
